newsitem.title: USA: Grand Casinos Tunica gaming revenue rises.
newsitem.headline: Grand Casinos Tunica gaming revenue rises.

text.p: Grand Casinos said Tuesday its Grand Casino Tunica in Mississippi had gaming revenue totaling $33.2 million for the first quarter, up 20.7 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996.
No first quarter 1996 comparison for Tunica was available. The facility opened in mid-1996.

"We are very pleased with the improved results at Grand Casino Tunica and are encouraged by the initial response we have received to the new hotel located on our 2,100-acre resort site adjacent to the casino complex," Lyle Berman, chairman, said in a statement.
He added that all Grand Casino properties performed well in the first quarter, despite bad weather in all markets and major expansion projects at several locations.
Although the Grand Veranda Hotel at Tunica operated for only 25 days of the quarter, occupancy of 77 percent was achieved at an average daily rate of approximately $50, the company said.
Occupancy at the Grand Casino Hotel, Grand Casino Tunica's 188-room hotel connected to the casino complex, was 94 percent with an average daily rate of $58 for the quarter.

Earlier, Grand Casino reported first quarter earnings of $0.34 a share, down from $0.41 a year ago. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rose 25.1 percent to $42.4 million, it added.
Management fee income from Grand Casinos' four managed properties increased to $19.1 million from $18.8 million in the first quarter of 1996.
As a result of the company writing off its investment in Stratosphere Corp in the fourth quarter, Grand Casinos no longer recognizes any effect from Stratosphere operations.
